title: 9 Best Klear Alternatives for 2026
summary: Klear is now "Meltwater Influencer Marketing" — Enterprise-tier only, plus a $10K-25K/yr module fee. Compare all 9 alternatives, including Syncly.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** "Klear" no longer exists as a product you can buy. As of an April 2024 rebrand, it's "Meltwater Influencer Marketing" — available only at Meltwater's Enterprise tier (starting around $130,000/year) or on Agency plans, and explicitly excluded from the Starter ($10,000/year) and Pro ($25,000/year) configurations (Source:[Meltwater, Meltwater Pricing: Plans, Ranges & What to Expect, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/meltwater-pricing) ). The influencer module itself adds a further $10,000-$25,000/year on top of whichever base tier you land on (Source:[Creator Hero, Meltwater Pricing and Review, 2026](https://www.creator-hero.com/blog/meltwater-pricing-and-review) ). CreatorIQ and Traackr cover the same enterprise tier as a purchasable core product rather than a bundled module. GRIN, Aspire, and Upfluence give ecommerce brands a dedicated off-ramp at a fraction of the cost. Modash and HypeAuditor cover budget discovery and fraud verification. Captiv8 offers comparable enterprise scale that, unlike Klear, isn't folded into an unrelated PR suite. None of them, Klear included, analyzes what a creator actually said or did inside a video — Klear's Visual Search matches on image style, not audio, speech, or motion across a timeline.


Type "klear.com" into a browser today and you land on Meltwater's site with a utm_medium=klear tag quietly capturing the leftover brand search. That's not a broken link — it's the entire product now. Klear was acquired by Meltwater in 2021, and in April 2024 it was formally folded into "Meltwater Influencer Marketing" (Source:[Storika, Storika vs. Klear (Meltwater), 2026](https://www.storika.ai/compare/storika-vs-klear) ), a module that only exists inside Meltwater's Enterprise or Agency tiers. If your team just wants a dedicated tool to find and vet creators, you can no longer buy that as its own thing from this vendor — you buy into a PR-and-social-monitoring suite first. This post breaks down what that bundling actually costs, and where nine alternatives let a team buy creator discovery without the rest of it. It's built around[content-first creator discovery](https://syncly.app/blog/content-first-creator-discovery-beauty) .


## What does Klear (now Meltwater Influencer Marketing) do well — and where does it strain?


Klear's strongest asset survived the rebrand intact: Visual Search, an AI image-matching layer that finds creators by a text prompt, an uploaded reference image, or a past campaign's visual style — and as of 2026 it extends into YouTube Discovery, letting a user describe an "ideal video" in words to surface matching creators (Source:[Meltwater, Meltwater Influencer Marketing User Guide, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/meltwater-influencer-marketing-user-guide-klear) ). Named customers span consumer brands genuinely worth citing — Unilever ran a multi-country Persil "Dirt is Good" micro-influencer search through it, alongside Canon, Western Union, Microsoft, and Mailchimp (Source:[Klear, Persil Success Story](https://klear.com/success-stories/persil) ). Capterra reviewers rate the product 4.3/5 across 13 verified reviews as of this writing (Source:[Capterra, Klear Reviews, 2026](https://www.capterra.com/p/175484/Klear/reviews/) ) — a thin sample, but consistent with a generally capable tool. For a narrower comparison of Klear specifically against Upfluence and Traackr on contract terms, see our[Upfluence vs Klear vs Traackr breakdown](https://syncly.app/blog/upfluence-vs-klear-vs-traackr) .


Where it strains is structural, not qualitative. Meltwater's own pricing page states plainly that influencer marketing "isn't part of the Starter or Pro configurations" — it's Enterprise-tier-only, or available on Agency plans (Source:[Meltwater, Meltwater Pricing, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/meltwater-pricing) ). A brand that wants only creator discovery ends up paying for, onboarding into, and maintaining four other bundled solution areas — PR monitoring, social listening, media relations, AI visibility — that it never asked for. Search-aggregated sources put Klear's legacy G2 listing at roughly 4.2/5, down from the ~4.5/5 figure cited in earlier comparisons, though G2 blocks automated verification of the exact current figure, so treat that number as directional rather than confirmed.


## Why do brands look for a Klear alternative in the first place?


Six friction points recur across Meltwater's own pricing documentation, third-party buyer research, and independent "Meltwater alternatives" content: forced bundling into an enterprise suite, a real incremental module cost on top of an already expensive base tier, an aggressive renewal and sales process, below-average value-for-money ratings, database size limits, and an interface built for PR teams rather than agile marketing teams.


-


**The "suite tax":** you cannot buy influencer discovery alone. One third-party analysis found "pure-play influencer teams frequently find themselves paying five-figure annual fees for massive, eight-product systems when they only use the platform to search, vet, and manage content creators" (Source:[Influencity, Unbundling the PR Suite, 2026](https://influencity.com/blog/en/top-3-alternatives-to-meltwater-for-influencer-marketing) ).


-


**A real incremental module cost:** the influencer marketing add-on runs an estimated $10,000-$25,000/year on top of a base subscription that itself starts around $10,000/year for Starter, $25,000/year for Pro, and $130,000/year for Enterprise (Source:[Creator Hero, Meltwater Pricing and Review, 2026](https://www.creator-hero.com/blog/meltwater-pricing-and-review) ;[Meltwater, Meltwater Pricing, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/meltwater-pricing) ).


-


**No published rate card, aggressive renewal process:** pricing is quote-only and annual-contract, and reviewer analysis describes "aggressive upselling and 'gotcha' renewal practices," with multiple G2, Trustpilot, and BBB reviews citing difficulty exiting contracts and auto-renewal terms with 3-7% annual escalations (Source:[Creator Hero, 2026](https://www.creator-hero.com/blog/meltwater-pricing-and-review) ;[NC Media Group, Meltwater Pricing and Review, 2026](https://nc-media-group.com/blog-posts/meltwater-pricing-and-review) ).


-


**Value-for-money below the category average:** Meltwater holds ratings of roughly 3.9-4.1/5 on G2, but only 3.4/5 for value specifically on Capterra (Source:[NC Media Group, 2026](https://nc-media-group.com/blog-posts/meltwater-pricing-and-review) ).


-


**Database size constraints:** Meltwater's influencer discovery database (powered by the former Klear) runs roughly 30 million creator profiles — smaller than several specialized discovery platforms built after it (Source:[Influencity, 2026](https://influencity.com/blog/en/top-3-alternatives-to-meltwater-for-influencer-marketing) ).


-


**Interface built for PR workflows, not marketing agility:** because the tools sit inside a legacy media-intelligence suite, "the user interface can feel clunky and disjointed for non-PR users," with basic searches often requiring Boolean-string setup (Source:[Influencity, 2026](https://influencity.com/blog/en/top-3-alternatives-to-meltwater-for-influencer-marketing) ).


## How do the 9 Klear alternatives compare on price and discovery method?


Eight of the nine platforms below match on bio keywords, audience demographics, or purchase and brand-affinity data. Klear is the exception that searches something else: static image style. Only Syncly searches the actual content of a video.


**Database/metadata search** : creator discovery that matches on profile fields — bio keywords, audience demographics, follower counts, hashtags, and purchase or brand-affinity signals. This is how CreatorIQ, GRIN, Aspire, Upfluence, Traackr, Modash, HypeAuditor, and Captiv8 all work.


**Visual Search (Klear/Meltwater)** : an image-analysis layer that matches creators to a text prompt, an uploaded reference image, or a past campaign's visual style — extended into YouTube Discovery in 2026 to accept a written description of an "ideal video." It's the most content-adjacent mechanism in this comparison outside Syncly, but it's still style and image matching, not a transcript or scene-level read of a video's actual audio and speech.


**Content-first creator discovery (Syncly)** : indexes the actual spoken audio, on-screen text, and visuals inside a creator's past videos — including brand or topic mentions never typed into a bio, caption, or hashtag. This is how Syncly Creator Discovery works.

## The 9 Best Klear Alternatives


### 1. Syncly Creator Discovery


Syncly Creator Discovery indexes the actual content of a creator's past videos and posts — visuals, speech, on-screen text, and untagged brand mentions — instead of matching on bio metadata or image style alone (Source:[Syncly Creator Discovery](https://syncly.app/social/solution/creator-discovery) ). That runs on Syncly's[video analysis](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) engine: where Klear's Visual Search answers "which creators' photos look like this?", Syncly answers "which creators have actually said, shown, or done this in a video?" It's also sold as its own product, not a module gated behind an enterprise PR suite. Pricing: custom — free trial.


### 2. CreatorIQ


CreatorIQ is the direct enterprise-tier peer for a brand leaving Klear's spend bracket, but purchasable as its actual core product rather than a bundled add-on. Its ~22M-profile database runs through a LiveRamp partnership, with brand-safety tooling (SafeIQ) and benchmarking (BenchmarkIQ) across 37 markets. Annual contracts run roughly $30,000-$200,000+, median around $39,250 (Source:[Archive.com, CreatorIQ Pricing, 2026](https://archive.com/blog/creatoriq-pricing) ). Named customers include LVMH, Sephora, Nestlé, Google, and Delta.


### 3. GRIN


GRIN is the ecommerce-native alternative: native Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, and BigCommerce integrations, plus Gia, GRIN's agentic AI assistant handling outreach drafting and content triage across 700K+ transaction-verified creators with 180-attribute fit scoring. GRIN opened a free self-serve affiliate tier in January 2026, while mid-market annual contracts still run $25,000-$100,000/year (Source:[GRIN, self-serve launch, 2026](https://grin.co/news/grin-launches-self-serve-creator-marketing/) ). See our[GRIN alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/grin-alternatives-for-influencer-discovery) for a deeper look.


### 4. Aspire


Aspire runs on inbound: brands post campaign briefs to 1M+ opted-in creators and manage the full workflow — briefs, product seeding, content review, payment — in one place, with zero commission taken from the creator side. Pricing starts around $2,000/month with an annual commitment. Named customers include Glossier, Bombas, Coola, and Ruggable. See our[Aspire alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/aspire-alternatives-for-influencer-discovery) for how it compares against this same set.


### 5. Upfluence


Upfluence is the pick for ecommerce brands selling across more than one storefront, with a native Amazon integration alongside Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce — no competitor in this list matches that combination. Entry pricing starts around $478/month, with most ecommerce brands landing between $795 and $1,750/month on a 12-month contract. Its Jaice AI layer interprets creator content-behavior patterns on top of standard keyword and demographic filtering, though that's still metadata-adjacent rather than true video-content search.


### 6. Traackr


Traackr is the other enterprise-tier peer worth naming alongside CreatorIQ — built for benchmarking and spend optimization across a global creator program, and, like CreatorIQ, purchasable on its own terms rather than as a module inside a bigger suite. Pricing runs $25,000-$55,000+/year, annual-only with no free trial. Its named case studies are specific: Laneige saw a 951% increase in Traackr's proprietary VIT metric between 2021 and 2024. See our[Traackr alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/traackr-alternatives-for-2026) for a closer look at this same peer set.


### 7. Modash


Modash is the budget entry point: a searchable database with a 14-day free trial and no card required. Essentials starts at $199/month for 100 tracked creators, Performance at $499/month for 250. Its 4.9/5 G2 rating looks strong, but it's built on just 15-19 reviews — a much thinner sample than the other platforms here, worth factoring into how much weight that score carries.


### 8. HypeAuditor


HypeAuditor's core job is verification: auditing influencer and audience authenticity across a large profile database spanning Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Twitch, and X before a brand commits budget — the same problem our[influencer verification tools](https://syncly.app/blog/best-influencer-verification-tools) roundup digs into more broadly. Basic runs around $299/month and Pro around $499/month, both billed annually. G2 reviewers rate it 4.6/5, with 35+ fraud-detection metrics as its distinctive strength.


### 9. Captiv8


Captiv8 is the closest thing to a like-for-like swap for a brand leaving an enterprise PR-adjacent bundle: a genuinely distinctive AI-powered Media/Brand Safety layer scanning 300M+ external media sources for risk scoring, plus a Perplexity-powered AI Q&A layer added in 2025. It's also the one platform on this list that, like Klear, recently changed hands — Publicis Groupe acquired it in 2025 — but it remains purchasable as a dedicated creator marketing product rather than a module bolted onto an unrelated suite. Entry pricing runs around $25,000/year plus a $3,000 onboarding fee, with no self-serve tier. For the full breakdown, see our[Captiv8 alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/captiv8-alternatives-for-2026) .


## Key Takeaways


-


Klear no longer exists as a standalone product — it was formally rebranded "Meltwater Influencer Marketing" in April 2024, and klear.com now redirects straight to Meltwater's suite page.


-


Influencer marketing is Enterprise-tier-only per Meltwater's own pricing page, excluded from Starter ($10K/yr) and Pro ($25K/yr), adding $10,000-$25,000/year on top once you're in Enterprise (~$130K/yr) or Agency plans.


-


Klear's Visual Search remains genuinely distinctive — image and style matching via text prompt or reference image — but it does not transcribe speech, read on-screen text, or analyze motion across a video, unlike Syncly Creator Discovery.


-


CreatorIQ and Traackr cover the same enterprise spend bracket but are purchasable as their actual core product, not a module inside a PR-and-social-monitoring suite.


-


None of these vendors publish official rate cards — treat every price point in this article as a third-party estimate, not a quote.


## Is it worth switching away from Klear?


If your team is already deep inside Meltwater's suite for PR monitoring and social listening, the influencer module riding along as a fifth bundled solution area is a reasonable trade-off — you're not paying for it in isolation. But if creator discovery is the only thing you actually use, or you were never in the Meltwater ecosystem to begin with, the case for switching is straightforward: you're paying enterprise-suite prices for a product you can no longer buy on its own. The right next tool depends on what you actually need — comparable enterprise scale without the bundling (CreatorIQ, Traackr, Captiv8), a lower ecommerce entry point (GRIN, Aspire, Upfluence), or a larger database for budget discovery or fraud checks (Modash, HypeAuditor). If the real gap is that your best creator candidates aren't searchable by image style or bio metadata at all — because the signal is in what they said or did on camera — that's a different problem, and it's the one[Syncly Creator Discovery](https://syncly.app/social/solution/creator-discovery/pricing) is built to solve.
